candidates.title: Two `#[allow(dead_code)]` attributes on `ParsedData` carry rationales naming consumers that do not exist: `penalties` is genuinely never read, `scalar_parameters` is read and the allow is stale

evidence.command: grep -rn 'data\.penalties' crates/ --include='*.rs' | wc -l; grep -n 'data\.scalar_parameters' crates/cobre-io/src/pipeline.rs; sed -n '70,75p;110,114p' crates/cobre-io/src/validation/schema.rs
evidence.reading: `data.penalties` has zero references workspace-wide, so the field at schema.rs:75 is dead in fact; its rationale names the Layer 5 penalty-ordering check, but that check (`scenarios::check_penalty_ordering` reached through `validate_semantic_stages_penalties_scenarios`) reads the per-entity `hydro.penalties` at crates/cobre-io/src/validation/semantic/scenarios.rs:179, and the only value the parsers receive is the local `sentinel` built at crates/cobre-io/src/validation/schema.rs:273 — nothing re-reads penalties.json, so the stated saving does not exist. The mirror case is the reverse: `scalar_parameters` IS read at crates/cobre-io/src/pipeline.rs:96 and moved at :244, so the `#[allow(dead_code)]` at schema.rs:113 suppresses a lint that would not fire. Both attributes therefore misdescribe the tree, and the mirror's `#[allow(...)]` census classifies every `dead_code` allow as a reserved seam whose comment names a future reader, which neither of these is.

candidates.fixShape: Split the two by fact. For `penalties`, decide the field's fate rather than annotating it: either delete the field and its construction at schema.rs:669 (the sentinel already carries every value any parser needs), or, if the global defaults genuinely belong in the bundle for a future check, register it as a reserved seam in the mirror with an owner and a consuming milestone, and rewrite the comment to name the reader that will land instead of asserting one that already exists. For `scalar_parameters`, delete the `#[allow(dead_code)]` outright and let the comment shrink to the one fact worth keeping, since the field is a live consumer of the pipeline's own call. Whichever way `penalties` goes, the four `ParsedData` literal constructors in the test modules (validation/dimensional.rs, validation/productivity_resolution.rs, validation/semantic/test_support.rs, validation/semantic/travel_time.rs) are the full blast radius.

candidates.title: `ErrorKind::default_severity` is a public severity classification with zero callers, and it already disagrees with the call sites it purports to describe

evidence.command: grep -rnw 'default_severity' crates/ --include='*.rs'; grep -rn -A1 'ctx.add_warning(' crates/cobre-io/src --include='*.rs' | grep -oP 'ErrorKind::\K[A-Za-z]+' | sort | uniq -c
evidence.reading: The only references to `default_severity` anywhere in crates/ are its own declaration and the four assertions of its own unit test at validation/mod.rs:419-429; it is the single symbol in the whole sub-station that a per-symbol external-reference sweep found with no reference outside its declaring file. Severity is instead chosen explicitly at every diagnostic site by calling `add_error` (validation/mod.rs:157) or `add_warning` (:174), so the method is a second, never-consulted classification of the fifteen `ErrorKind` variants. It has already drifted from the sites: `default_severity` maps every kind except UnusedEntity / ModelQuality / SemanticAmbiguity to `Severity::Error`, yet one live call site emits `BusinessRuleViolation` as a warning at crates/cobre-io/src/validation/semantic/season.rs:175-177. Because nothing reads the method, that disagreement is invisible and cannot fail anything.

candidates.fixShape: Delete the method and its tautological unit test, leaving `add_error` / `add_warning` as the single owner of severity. If a per-kind default is actually wanted, invert the direction instead of deleting: make the table the one that decides, by routing every diagnostic through a single `add` entry point that consults the kind, and turn the `season.rs` warning into a deliberate documented override rather than a silent divergence. Either way the classification should exist once. Blast radius is the two items in validation/mod.rs plus, in the second shape only, the roughly thirty-three `add_warning` call sites across validation/semantic/.

candidates.title: `FileManifest` presence tracking is three hand-maintained 43-element lists zipped positionally, with a hand-rolled `[&mut bool; 43]` reflection helper and only a length guard

evidence.command: grep -c 'FileEntry {' crates/cobre-io/src/validation/structural.rs; grep -c '&mut m\.' crates/cobre-io/src/validation/structural.rs; grep -c 'pub [a-z_]*: bool,' crates/cobre-io/src/validation/structural.rs; sed -n '376p;396,398p;614,622p' crates/cobre-io/src/validation/structural.rs
evidence.reading: Three lists describe the same 43 input files and must stay in the same order: 43 `pub bool` fields on `FileManifest`, 43 `FileEntry` rows in `FILE_ENTRIES` (the 44th match is the struct declaration itself), and 43 `&mut m.<field>` entries returned by `manifest_fields_mut`. `validate_structure` at :376 joins lists two and three by position. The helper's own doc at :396-397 states the hazard — a divergence silently misassigns presence flags — and the only guard, the test at :614-622, compares lengths and says so in its own comment: the invariant is length, not order. Since 38 of the 43 rows are optional, swapping any two of them keeps both the length test and the eight-missing-required-files test green while every downstream presence check reads the wrong file's flag. The middle list buys nothing on its own: it exists solely so a struct of named bools can be iterated, which is hand-rolled reflection rather than a data structure.

candidates.fixShape: Collapse the three lists to one by making the file table the single declaration and deriving both the storage and the accessors from it. The shape that keeps the named, type-checked reads the 34 call sites in validation/schema.rs depend on is a single ordered table of files paired with an enum key, with the manifest holding one flag array indexed by that key and named accessor methods generated alongside it, so adding a file is one edit and a mis-order is a compile error rather than a silent misassignment. A lighter variant that keeps the struct as-is is to make the zip key on the path string instead of position, so the table drives assignment by name and `manifest_fields_mut` disappears. Either way the change is behaviour-neutral for a correctly ordered tree; blast radius is structural.rs plus the 38 manifest reads in validation/schema.rs. This is a distinct site from the cut-projection gather axes the mirror's Cleared section records as having no unfixed positional-zip sibling.

candidates.title: Three hand-written `Deserialize` impls in `config/` reimplement what `#[derive(Deserialize)]` already produces, each duplicating its accepted-value list

evidence.command: grep -rn "impl<'de> .*Deserialize<'de> for" crates/cobre-io/src/config/; sed -n '12,15p' crates/cobre-io/src/config/policy.rs; sed -n '962,966p' crates/cobre-io/src/system/hydros.rs
evidence.reading: All three are unit-variant enums carrying `#[serde(rename_all = "snake_case")]` whose hand-written impl does exactly one thing: deserialize a `String`, match the snake_case spellings, and return `unknown_variant(other, &[..])`. That is the derive's own behaviour — `PolicyMode` at config/policy.rs:15 is the structural twin in the same directory and derives it, and the crate documents the derived message shape it relies on at system/hydros.rs:965 (`unknown variant 'foo', expected one of …`), which is what `extract_field_from_serde_msg` at config/mod.rs:129-133 keys on. So the requirement the three tests pin (`unknown_scheme_is_rejected_naming_accepted_set`, `unknown_stopping_mode_is_rejected_naming_accepted_set`, `order_selection_unknown_variant_lists_pacf_annual` in config/mod.rs) is met by the derive without the impl. The cost is that each accepted-value list is now written twice per enum, in the match arms and again in the slice passed to `unknown_variant`, plus a third time in the doc comment, with nothing tying them together. The commit that introduced them (fa667340, promoting six bare-string discriminators to real serde enums) records no reason for hand-writing rather than deriving.

candidates.fixShape: Replace each hand-written impl with `Deserialize` in the existing derive list, leaving `rename_all` and the doc comments as the single spelling declaration, and keep the three accepted-set rejection tests exactly as they are so the change is proved behaviour-preserving rather than asserted. One honest difference has to be checked before landing it: the hand-written version accepts only a bare JSON string, while the derived one also accepts serde's single-key-map form for a unit variant, so if narrowing to strings was the unstated intent, the right fix is the opposite direction — keep one impl, document the narrowing in a single clause, and delete the other two by deriving them, rather than leaving three undocumented copies. Blast radius is the three declaring files.

positives.subject: crates/cobre-io/src/schema.rs::generate_schemas

One owner declares all eighteen input-file schemas in a single vec; the two consumers (crates/cobre-cli/src/commands/schema.rs:64 and crates/cobre-python/src/schema.rs:43) are thin pass-throughs with no second list; `ls schemas/ | wc -l` is 18, matching the vec exactly; and the eighteen entries are precisely the eighteen hand-authored JSON files in `FILE_ENTRIES`, with no gap and no orphan. positives.why: The 129 `feature = "schema"` sites are not rotting. `CARGO_TARGET_DIR=<scratch> cargo check -p cobre-io --no-default-features` finished with exit code 0 at the baseline, so the gate that no CI job exercises still compiles.

_needsHuman: Both entry-point crates pin `cobre-io` with `features = ["schema"]` and every CI job lists `schema` in NON_SOLVER_FEATURES, so no build in the repo ever compiles the off-state of the 129-site feature gate; whether that optional-dependency seam still earns its keep is an owner call, because cobre-io is a published crate whose external consumers are not visible from here.

The rustdoc table at crates/cobre-io/src/schema.rs:50-69 restates all eighteen schema filenames and their source files with nothing comparing it to the vec below it, and the unit test at :262-276 asserts only thirteen of the eighteen names are present; whether that gap deserves a gate or is acceptable doc-only duplication needs the owner.

`crates/cobre-io/src/validation/semantic/season.rs:175-177` emits `ErrorKind::BusinessRuleViolation` as a warning while the module rule table (validation/semantic/mod.rs, Layer 5b rule 31) prints it as `BusinessRuleViolation` with no warning marker; deciding whether the rule is meant to be advisory or blocking is a domain call, not an over-engineering one.
